<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   - This is an open-source Python library (“linkedin_scraper”) whose sole purpose is to scrape LinkedIn data (Person, Company, Job, JobSearch) via Selenium WebDriver.
   - The README makes clear it’s a library/package (install via pip), with APIs (Person, Company, Job, JobSearch) and helper module (actions) to log in.

2. Analyze the file structure
   - Top-level package: linkedin_scraper/
     • actions.py       – login helper  
     • selectors.py     – CSS/XPath selector definitions  
     • constants.py     – static values (timeouts, URLs)  
     • company.py       – Company scraper class  
     • person.py        – Person scraper class  
     • job_search.py    – JobSearch scraper class  
     • jobs.py          – Job scraper class  
     • objects.py       – data model objects (Experience, Education, etc.)  
   - samples/           – example usage scripts  
   - test/              – unit tests for core scraping methods  
   - setup.py, requirements.txt – package/build config  

3. Examine the README for additional insights
   - Dependencies: selenium, chromedriver (set via CHROMEDRIVER env var)  
   - Usage flow: optional actions.login → instantiate Person/Company/Job/JobSearch with driver → call .scrape()  
   - Extensibility: user can pass their own WebDriver; can choose to close browser or reuse it.

4. Drawing the system design diagram
   a. Main components
      • Client Application (your script or interactive session)  
      • linkedin_scraper Library  
        – API Layer: Person, Company, Job, JobSearch classes  
        – Helper Layer: actions.login  
        – Core Layer: selectors, constants, objects  
      • Selenium WebDriver (ChromeDriver)  
      • External System: LinkedIn Web Application  
   b. Relationships & interactions
      1. Client code calls API Layer (e.g., Person(url, driver))  
      2. If login required, actions.login(driver, email, password) authenticates to LinkedIn  
      3. API Layer uses WebDriver to navigate to LinkedIn URLs  
      4. WebDriver retrieves page HTML  
      5. Core Layer (selectors + constants) extracts data from DOM  
      6. objects.py constructs domain objects and returns them to the client  
   c. Architectural patterns & design principles
      • Separation of concerns:  
        – actions handles authentication  
        – selectors/constants hold parsing logic separate from workflows  
        – objects.py strictly defines data models  
      • Dependency injection: client provides own WebDriver  
      • No persistent storage—stateless, in-memory scraping  
   d. Key technologies/frameworks
      • Python packaging: setup.py, requirements.txt  
      • Selenium WebDriver (ChromeDriver)  
      • CSS/XPath for selectors  

5. Guidelines for an open-source scraping tool diagram
   - Focus on core functionality: clearly show the scraping workflow from client → library → WebDriver → LinkedIn → back.  
   - Highlight extensibility points: passing custom WebDriver, toggling close_on_complete, login hook.  
   - Show integration boundaries: library vs. external Selenium vs. LinkedIn website.

6. Diagramming elements to include
   - Boxes for components: label them (Client, API Layer, Helper Layer, Core Layer, WebDriver, LinkedIn)  
   - Directed arrows:  
     • “calls” from Client → API Layer  
     • “uses” from API Layer → actions.login  
     • “navigates to” from WebDriver → LinkedIn  
     • “parses with” from Core Layer ← page HTML  
   - Color/shape coding:  
     • Blue for internal modules (API, helpers, core)  
     • Green for external dependencies (WebDriver)  
     • Orange for external systems (LinkedIn website)  
   - Include notes on environment variables (CHROMEDRIVER) and configuration files.

7. Emphasize detail
   - Diagram every module (actions, selectors, constants, objects, each scraper class)  
   - Mark their interactions in sequence (login → navigate → scrape → return data)  
   - Don’t lump everything into “scraper”; show separations to aid maintenance and future extension.

By following these steps, you’ll produce a clear, detailed system design diagram tailored to the linkedin_scraper project, highlighting its architecture, data flow, and extensibility points.  
</explanation>
